questions.explain: The chapter maps classical ML and statistical models (time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, classification) to structured metric streams, while LLMs handle reasoning/explanation and embeddings handle semantic search.
options: Large Language Models (LLMs)
Classical ML and statistical models
Embedding models and vector search
Prompt engineering frameworks
questions.q: According to the chapter, which AI capability layer is best suited for metric-based prediction and anomaly detection on streams like CPU, IOPS, and wait event distributions?

questions.explain: The read vs. write boundary requires AI systems to read telemetry freely but never execute DDL, DML, or configuration changes without a human approval gate or validated automated testing gate.
options: AI must use only approved LLM model families
AI must not be given access to Query Store data
AI must be able to read telemetry but not execute DDL, DML, or configuration changes without a human approval gate
AI must run only on the database server itself
questions.q: Under the chapter's governance principles, which AI action boundary is described as non-negotiable in the early stages of AI integration?

questions.explain: LLMs excel at reasoning, explanation, and code generation, but they are not suited to real-time anomaly detection where sub-second latency matters and they are not trained on your specific production telemetry.
options: They are not trained on your specific production telemetry and cannot meet sub-second latency requirements
They cannot read T-SQL at all
They are unable to process numeric metrics
They only work with the database they were trained on
questions.q: Why does the chapter state that LLMs are poorly suited to real-time anomaly detection?

questions.explain: Prompt auditability requires logging every LLM prompt and response with a timestamp, model version, token count, and the context that triggered the call, paralleling the change logs DBAs maintain for manual actions.
options: Deleting all prompts after each API call to save storage
Logging every prompt and response with timestamp, model version, token count, and triggering context
Sending prompts only through unencrypted channels
Allowing any model version without tracking which was used
questions.q: Which practice is part of the chapter's 'prompt auditability' principle?

questions.explain: The extract-enrich-route pattern is the building block for all the more sophisticated AI database operations systems in the book: telemetry out, AI analysis in the middle, structured results routed to ticketing or alerting.
options: Replace the database engine with an LLM endpoint
Extract telemetry from the database, enrich it with AI analysis, and route the structured result to an operations workflow
Send raw production data to a public LLM with no logging
Manually run every AI recommendation with no automation
questions.q: What is the foundational integration pattern the chapter describes as recurring throughout the book?

title: The Evolution of the DBA in the AI Era
